## 391145: odd cycles spanning high chromatic number

The literal quantifies over every k>=3 and every sufficiently high-chromatic finite graph. A large odd cycle alone is insufficient: its induced graph may still be 3-colorable. The original UCSD problem artifact was unavailable after a TLS certificate failure. The downloaded Chung collection's reciprocal-odd-length question is a DIFFERENT problem and supplies no solution to this literal. Search-mentioned Gyárfás Fruit Salad and Steiner path equivalence are navigation only; their actual bodies were not acquired.

Route A, breadth-first levels and parity, reaches a precise equivalent obstacle. Define the path-span forcing assertion P(r): there is an integer M(r) such that every finite graph of chromatic number at least M(r) contains a simple path whose vertex-induced subgraph has chromatic number at least r. Suppose P(r) holds for every r. Let k>=3 and a connected graph G have chi(G)>=2M(k+1). Partition a BFS tree into levels L_i. Edges join equal or consecutive levels; color each even level with one palette and each odd level with a disjoint palette. Thus chi(G)<=2 max_i chi(G[L_i]). Some level L has chromatic number at least M(k+1). Apply P(k+1) inside it, obtaining path Q whose span has chromatic number >=k+1. If Q has an odd number of edges, retain Q. Otherwise delete one endpoint. The remaining path P has odd edge length, and deleting one vertex decreases chi by at most one, so chi(G[V(P)])>=k. It has distinct endpoints u,v in L (k>=3 prevents a trivial path). Their tree paths to the root meet first at their least common ancestor w, strictly below level L. The u-w and v-w paths are internally disjoint, meet L only at their endpoints, and have equal lengths. Their union is an even-length u-v path R with all internal vertices outside L. Consequently P union R is a simple odd cycle. Its induced span contains the span of P and has chi>=k. Disconnected G is handled by a component of maximum chromatic number. This is a complete conditional bridge; it does not prove P.

Conversely, if the literal odd-cycle forcing assertion holds for every k, then P(r) follows by choosing an odd cycle with span chi>=r and dropping one CYCLE EDGE, leaving a simple path on the same vertices. No loss of chromatic number occurs in this direction, because chromatic number is measured in G induced on the vertices, not only along path edges. Thus the all-k path-span assertion and literal are equivalent. The forward proof pays parity and the lower-level closure explicitly. It remains a helper equivalent reformulation, with no novelty claim (a related equivalence is specifically mentioned in search).

Route B, DFS/critical graphs: a vertex-critical r-chromatic graph has minimum degree >=r-1, but DFS only puts back edges on ancestor chains; it does not bound the chromatic number of the union by the maximum chromatic number of those chains. An ancestor may occur in many branches, so independently coloring each chain does not give compatible colors on their overlaps. A longest path's length or a critical graph's minimum degree supplies no bound for chi of its induced span. The missing lemma is exactly uniform chi-boundedness of graphs all of whose path spans have bounded chi. Neither minimum degree nor odd girth pays it. No claimed counterexample family is available: high girth controls short cycles, not every odd cycle's induced chromatic number. Park full target.

## 390745: clique transversals

Write q(G)=max{|S|: S contains no inclusion-maximal clique of G of size>=2}. Complementation gives tau(G)=n-q(G): a complement meets each such clique exactly when S contains none. The actual Chung problem (71), printed p18, states the target using R(n) and reports only tau<=n-sqrt(2n)+c; this source uses abbreviated 'clique' terminology. The literal's maximal/nontrivial convention is retained throughout our arguments.

Route A, neighborhoods and independent sets. N(v) contains no maximal clique of G: any clique entirely in N(v) could be enlarged by v. Hence q(G)>=Delta(G). Every independent set also contains no clique of size>=2, hence q(G)>=alpha(G). Greedy coloring with Delta+1 colors gives alpha(G)>=n/(Delta+1): order vertices arbitrarily and give each the first color unused by its already colored neighbors; at most Delta colors are forbidden. Therefore q(G)>=max{Delta,n/(Delta+1)}, giving a square-root lower bound on q. This does not reach H(n), whose sqrt(n log n) scale is reported by the actual source. Optimizing over Delta cannot manufacture the logarithm. In triangle-free G, the maximal nontrivial cliques are precisely edges, q(G)=alpha(G)>=H(n), giving the source-known case only. Sparse neighborhoods might permit independent-set bounds, but the arbitrary graph can have dense neighborhoods; no uniform local sparsity hypothesis is present.

Route B, triangle-free spanning subgraph. A sufficient stronger assertion is existence of a triangle-free graph F on the same vertex set, with E(F) subset E(G), such that every maximal nontrivial clique K of G contains an edge of F. Then an independent set of F of size H(n) cannot contain any such K, proving q(G)>=H(n). Merely take a maximal triangle-free subgraph is NOT a proof of the asserted property. The six-vertex 3-sun demonstrates the mechanism failure without any enumeration: start with triangle a,b,c and independent vertices x,y,z with neighborhoods {a,b},{b,c},{c,a}. F consists of the six edges xa,xb,yb,yc,zc,za, a 6-cycle. F is triangle-free; each omitted G-edge ab,bc,ca closes respectively a triangle via x,y,z. Thus F is inclusion-maximal among triangle-free subgraphs of G, yet misses all three edges of maximal clique {a,b,c}. A different choice of F could work; this is a failed mechanism, not a target counterexample.

Route C, induction on a removed clique. If a clique is deleted, maximal cliques of the induced remainder can differ from the original maximal cliques. An independent or clique-free subset in the remainder need not remain clique-free after adding several vertices back: a formerly extendible clique may become one of the forbidden original cliques. The required exchange would need to preserve every maximal-clique constraint AND recover the exact increment H(n)-H(n-r); no such exchange was proved. An inclusion-maximal admissible S gives for each outside vertex v a clique K_v subset S union {v} containing v, but these witnesses can overlap arbitrarily. They do not automatically define a triangle-free obstruction graph with independence <=|S|. This is the exact unpaid simultaneous selection lemma. Park full target, rather than call the helper or six-vertex example a resolution.

## 391292: balanced rainbow classification

The actual Axenovich-Clemen arXiv2209.13867v2 (28 Nov2022) defines complete balance as per-color degree (n-1)/m and directly states the universal question in Question1.1. This equals the literal floor(n/m) for n congruent1 modulo m. Read Sections1-4 including Lemmas2.1,2.2,3.1,3.2,4.1 and proofs; outside Sidon/perfect-difference-set/Peluse input statements were read as quoted, their original proofs were not audited. Figures1-3 are illustrative, not visually inspected. A full classification of ALL graphs is not supplied by those theorems.

Positive greedy route, paid but only forests: fix any forest F with v vertices and m>=1 edges. Assign its edges arbitrary distinct colors from the m-color palette. Root each component. Embed one root at a time, and embed each child after its parent. At a child step, its parent's neighbors of the prescribed color number d=(n-1)/m. Fewer than v vertices are already occupied. Thus if d>=v, an unoccupied neighbor exists. Roots and isolated vertices likewise use unoccupied vertices. This gives the exact rainbow forest for n>=mv+1 with n congruent1 modulo m, including disconnected forests. No cycle-closing condition is imposed by this argument. It is not a full classification or credited family.

Negative amplification route: the source's lexicographic product has constant per-color degree d_inner+n_inner*d_outer, so balance is preserved. A q-set meeting one cluster reduces to the inner coloring; a q-set meeting q distinct clusters reduces to the outer coloring; otherwise two vertices in one cluster and a third in another yield repeated colors. Thus no rainbow K_q is introduced. Iteration yields arbitrarily large completely balanced counterexamples in the appropriate congruence. This is the source-own proof, not new credit. The source's coordinate indexing in its displayed definition interchanges sizes; the verbal construction with outer n and inner m pays the intended formula without claiming a new correction result.

A universal replacement of the clique by arbitrary F fails in that mixed-cluster argument: F may have no vertex adjacent to both of the repeated-cluster vertices. Thus two equal colors in the ambient complete graph need not be colors of TWO EDGES OF F. Also when m=e(F) is even, an m-coloring with per-color degree1 on m+1 vertices is impossible (odd-order graph cannot have a perfect matching). This parity restriction is not a target refutation: other admissible orders can have even per-color degrees. Cycle-closing via intersections of two prescribed color neighborhoods is also unpaid: each has size (n-1)/m, and for m>=2 the elementary intersection lower bound 2(n-1)/m-n can be nonpositive.
